subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: How should OpenClaw treat legacy or migrated Telegram outbound queue rows whose previous `sendMessage` outcome is ambiguous but no `recoveryState` was recorded?
rationale: The code fix depends on an upgrade-policy choice: preserving delivery by replaying old rows risks duplicate visible Telegram messages, while quarantining or failing them may drop an unsent legacy message.

options.title: Quarantine Ambiguous Legacy Rows
options.body: Mark or move legacy Telegram rows with ambiguous network/timeout send evidence out of blind replay, preserving enough operator/doctor detail to inspect them later.

options.title: Require Exact Reconciliation Before Replay
options.body: Keep rows pending until a Telegram-capable reconciliation contract can prove whether the platform send landed, accepting that old entries may remain unresolved.

options.title: Accept Legacy Replay Risk
options.body: Leave legacy null-marker rows replayable and document the duplicate-delivery risk as an accepted upgrade tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Ambiguous Legacy Rows
recommendation.body: Mark or move legacy Telegram rows with ambiguous network/timeout send evidence out of blind replay, preserving enough operator/doctor detail to inspect them later.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the recovery split and merged the recent recovery-policy PRs, making this the strongest available owner for the upgrade semantics decision.
